articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Stroud, Washington among top options
articles.description: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール直前の補強候補：ストラウドやワシントンらが有力な選択肢に
articles.descriptionJa: 怪我やバイウィーク、厳しい対戦カードなどでラインナップの調整が必要な方に向けて、マット・ボーエンが潜在的な候補をリストアップします。
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

The Week 5 NFL schedule features some really tough matchups for fantasy football, starting with the quarterback position. However, I still have four options -- in the QB2 range -- who have some upside. There are also a handful of wide receivers below, including deeper-league fliers you can take a chance on. As always, we'll hit on the running back and tight ends, and I have two available defenses to stream this week.

Quarterbacks

 Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (33.3% rostered; at Patriots)

Cousins has scored 20 or more points in three straight games, and he has thrown two or more touchdown passes in all four games this season. Now, Cousins isn't going to provide any upside as a runner. We know that. But in Klint Kubiak's offense, one that leans on tight end usage, Cousins can play on rhythm. And the Raiders are going to throw the ball in scoring position, as Cousins' eight red zone touchdown passes are tied for second most in the league. He's a superflex starter in the road matchup versus the Patriots.

 C.J. Stroud, Houston Texans (41.1% rostered; at Titans)

Stroud benefited from the return of wide receiver Nico Collins in Week 4, producing a season-high 23.08 points in a prime matchup versus Dallas. Collins had 118 yards receiving, plus he scored two touchdowns on end zone throws. It's a much tougher matchup this week versus the Titans, but Stroud is scoring 17.1 PPG, and Collins is the difference-maker in the Houston route tree. Stroud has value here as a QB2 in superflex formats.

 Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (48.9% rostered; vs. Bears)

Love averages 16.2 fantasy PPG and has thrown two touchdown passes in all four games played. And due to a subpar rushing attack in Green Bay, Love is attempting 38.5 passes per game. Yes, the Bears defense ranks in the top 12 versus quarterbacks, but I do see positive perimeter matchups here for Packers wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. If you need a QB2 this week, Love does have some value.

 Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns (15.7% rostered; at Jets)

Watson (16.7 fantasy PPG) has scored 19 or more points in two of four games played, and he's averaging 31.8 rushing yards per game. The Jets defense ranks in the top five versus quarterbacks, so I don't love the matchup. However, if you need a QB2 with dual-threat upside Watson fits. We've seen the Browns take vertical shots in the pass game, so there is big-play potential for Watson.

articles.headline: How to ace your salary cap draft: Tips and strategies to build a winning team
articles.description: Are you ready for your salary cap draft? Jim McCormick lays out helpful strategies and tactics you can use to ace draft day.
articles.headlineJa: サラリーキャップ・ドラフトを攻略する方法：勝利チームを構築するためのヒントと戦略
articles.descriptionJa: サラリーキャップ・ドラフトの準備はできていますか？ジム・マコーミックが、ドラフト当日を成功させるために活用できる役立つ戦略と戦術を解説します。
articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is undeniably awesome. So is Victor Wembanyama. Yet, in a traditional snake draft, getting both is essentially impossible given both are found firmly in the first round.

There is a draft format, however, that absolutely allows you to pair SGA and Wemby. Or Nikola Jokic and Stephen Curry, Luka Doncic and Giannis Antetokounmpo ... you get the idea. Salary cap drafts afford you the ability to assemble compelling collections of superstars.

The mission of this piece isn't solely to explain how salary cap drafting works, but more importantly, share several actionable strategies to help you thrive in this uniquely rewarding way to build fantasy basketball rosters.

How a Salary Cap drafts work

In ESPN salary cap drafts, each manager begins with a $200 budget to build out their roster. Default settings host 13 roster spots, with the calculator on my laptop revealing this is a bit more than $15 per slot. You are welcome, of course, to spend well above $15 to acquire star-caliber players, leaving less for filler and depth.

Instead of having a fixed draft slot to acquire NBA talent as you would in a snake draft, managers rotate turns nominating players for bidding. As you might guess, the highest bidder when the clock hits zero lands that player on their respective roster. As my long-time colleague John Cregan once coined, "your reign as manager begins with a wad of fake cash, a couple of hours to kill, and an empty roster to stock."

Now that we have an idea how they operate, let's delve into some winning tips for salary cap drafts. The road to imaginary glory begins here.

Preparation pays

Leverage live draft trends as you prepare for your salary cap draft. Just like how we identify average draft position as a tool of differentiation and value in snake drafts, average salary performs this function in this format.

Unlike how we enter snake drafts knowing that certain players will get drafted in a finite range of selections, the variance and volatility of player pricing inherent to a salary draft demands you identify which players you truly want to target with your imaginary coin.

Which is to say, set not only price ranges you are willing to pay (within a few dollars) for specific NBA talents, but order players into pricing tiers.

If you are the turn in a snake draft, your options are almost surely limited to a handful of top talents available in that range. In salary formats, you can acquire two typical first-rounders, or four players generally found in the second and third rounds of snake results.

Before such expenditure, just make sure to have identified which talents in each tier you intend to bid for. In category-driven leagues, it's wise to prepare lists of players who thrive in distinct statistical categories; knowing that Cason Wallace is an elite, underrated source of steals. articles.headline: Don't be surprised if: Unsung heroes rack up the stats, and one QB to trade away
articles.description: Don't be surprised if the trade market for a QB1 drops off after Week 5, and unsung heroes start to shine.
articles.headlineJa: こうなる可能性あり：無名のヒーローたちが成績を伸ばし、放出を検討すべきQBが一人
articles.descriptionJa: 第5週以降にQB1のトレード市場が冷え込み、無名の選手たちが輝き始めても驚かないでください。
articles.body:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised!

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

Don't be surprised if ... Los Angeles Rams RB Kyren Williams finishes as a top 5 option

Williams, 25, is one of the rare running backs who consistently outperforms expectations and his ADP. He entered 2026 having surpassed 1,100 rushing yards in three consecutive seasons, with 13 or more total touchdowns each year and at least a top 10 fantasy finish. And still, he went 14th at his position in ESPN ADP.

The Rams gave the impression they weren't true believers, too, opting to draft Michigan's Blake Corum early in 2024 and handing him a significant role in Year 2. The Rams led the NFL in total yards last season, QB Matthew Stafford won league MVP honors and WR Puka Nacua was fantastic as always, but the Rams were also seventh in rushing yards.

The current version of Williams leads the Rams in fantasy points entering this Monday night at home against the defensively challenged Buffalo Bills. Only four defenses permit more fantasy points to running backs. Williams is on pace for his typical rushing numbers (230 carries, 1,250 yards, 13 touchdowns) but something has altered a bit.

Stafford is throwing the football toward Williams much more! Corum remains a factor on early downs, but Williams has 16 receptions for 137 yards on 20 targets the past two weeks. That is clearly new and important, and perhaps not a fluke. Perhaps the Rams did not think Williams was capable of this, but he is.

If the receiving work continues, Williams may deliver his best season yet. He caught 36 passes for 281 yards this past season (both career-bests) though he did see more work in the final weeks. Perhaps it was a harbinger. This year, he is pacing toward 89 receptions for 735 yards. He is already at 25 targets in four games, after earning 50 targets in 17 games last season! This is a positive trend, one which few considered on draft day.

Frankly, while San Francisco 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey sees massive reduction in his volume and statistical output, Williams is producing 2025's McCaffrey numbers and he is outscoring him by roughly four fantasy points per game this year. McCaffrey delivered 2,126 yards from scrimmage last season with 17 touchdowns. Williams is pacing toward 1,985 yards and 17 scores. OK, perhaps you never thought these players comparable, but look at the numbers.

After totaling a bloated and perhaps irresponsible 311 rushing attempts and 102 receptions last season, McCaffrey is on pace for only 213 rushes and 68 catches. articles.headline: Enzo Maresca: Man City titles not tainted by guilty verdict
articles.description: Enzo Maresca has said he would still have joined Manchester City as manager if he had known the club had been found guilty of breaching financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: エンツォ・マレスカ：マンチェスター・シティのタイトルは有罪判決で汚されることはない
articles.descriptionJa: エンツォ・マレスカは、クラブが財務規則違反で有罪判決を受けたことを知っていたとしても、それでも監督としてマンチェスター・シティに加入しただろうと語りました。
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca has said he would still have joined Manchester City as manager if he had known the club had been found guilty of breaching financial rules while insisting that none of the club's success under Abu Dhabi ownership has been tainted by the damning judgement.

Maresca faced reporters for the first time on Friday since the findings of the independent commission were published during the international break.

The Italian, who arrived early to his news conference and was smiling as he took his seat, answered questions for just under 16 minutes and was defiant throughout.

He insisted he had no regrets about taking the manager's job and defending his own achievements when he served as Pep Guardiola's assistant during City's treble season in 2022-23.

Asked whether he would have still agreed to take over from Guardiola had the verdict been released earlier, Maresca said: "100%, yes.

"I understand the reason why most of you [reporters] are here, but the only thing I can say is that it is something that I already said. There is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club. This is what I can say about that.

"I trust the club because I trust the people and this is also the reason why I joined the club. There is not another club in the world where I would like to be. I'm very happy to be, I'm very proud."

City have launched a formal appeal after being found guilty of multiple financial breaches between 2009 and 2018.

The verdict has raised questions about the legitimacy of all the success enjoyed since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008 -- including the treble won when Maresca was assistant.

- Man City 'a disgrace; I would throw them out' - furious Ian Holloway

- Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

But the 46-year-old rejected the suggestion his medals from success in the Premier League, Champions League and FA Cup in 2023 are tainted.

"Absolutely not," he said.

"The last time I was here was the Treble season and I know the effort from the players, the club, the manager. I know the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target so I don't have any doubt about that."

City face Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since the verdict was published. Maresca has welcomed his players back from international duty this week and said they're focused ahead of the trip to Anfield.

"We completely understand the seriousness of the situation," he said.

"We understand, the players understand, but it's our duty and our job to try to control the noise. The manager and the players are focused on winning games, not about something different."

Maresca offered a positive fitness update on Erling Haaland, who asked to be substituted for Norway during the international break.

Haaland was "good," his manager said, after a few days on holiday.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft QB rankings: Arch Manning, Dante Moore, Drew Mestemaker in top 15
articles.description: Who are the best quarterbacks in the 2027 draft class? We sized up the top 15, including Arch Manning, Dante Moore, Trinidad Chambliss and Darian Mensah.
articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフトQBランキング：アーチ・マンニング、ダンテ・ムーア、ドリュー・メステメーカーがトップ15入り
articles.descriptionJa: 2027年ドラフト候補の中で最高のクォーターバックは誰か？アーチ・マンニング、ダンテ・ムーア、トリニダード・チャンブリス、ダリアン・メンサを含むトップ15を評価しました。
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft class has been talked about in league circles for some time, and much of that discussion has centered on the perceived quality and depth of the quarterback group. How is that perception standing up as we inch closer to Round 1 in April in Washington, D.C.?

I've identified every quarterback who currently has a good chance to be drafted. This list goes 15 passers deep and includes information I've obtained in my conversations with scouts and front office personnel over the past couple of years. I'll go through the strengths and weaknesses of every QB, with updates on how they are faring in the 2026 college football season.

Let's get to it and stack the 15 best QBs in the 2027 class.

Jump to:

Day 2 picks | Day 3 picks

1. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State

Height: 6-foot-3 | Weight: 215 pounds

Class: Redshirt sophomore | Projected range: Round 1

Where he excels: Mestemaker's background is truly unique, as he transitioned from primarily being a punter and safety in high school to a walk-on quarterback at North Texas who entered the 2024 season sixth on the Mean Green's depth chart. He ascended rapidly and finished as the FBS leader in passing yards (4,379) in 2025.

After following coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State, NFL scouts were eager to see how Mestemaker would perform at the Power 4 level. So far, so good, as he has 1,271 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions in four games. Mestemaker struggled in his Oklahoma State debut against Tulsa in Week 1 but came up with a big performance against Oregon in Week 2, his first game against a Power 4 opponent. He finished 26-of-43 with 317 passing yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions while adding another 109 rushing yards and a score against what was expected to be one of the nation's best defenses.

Mestemaker has well-above-average arm strength and unconventional throwing mechanics, holding the ball near his waistline before using a three-quarters release. He's aggressive in hunting for explosive plays down the field; his 12 completions on passes of 20-plus air yards are tied for the most in the FBS. Mestemaker believes that he can fit passes into all types of windows, which leads to multiple "wow" throws that translate to the next level.

"Wild backstory and he has a little bit of an awkward release, but I see the vision," an AFC area scout said. "Outside of the Oregon game, he hasn't really played anyone, so I'm hoping we get to see him play in some meaningful football in the coming months."

Where he needs work: Mestemaker's overconfidence can lead to streakiness and to him spraying off-target passes, missing way outside the frame of wideouts. His biggest area of concern comes with underneath coverage, as he can be blind to shallow defenders. Bad eye discipline leads to him locking on to targets instead of reading coverage. articles.headline: Why the Raiders' running game has struggled, and what's next for Ashton Jeanty
articles.description: The Raiders have made offensive strides ... except for the running game. What's next for Las Vegas and Ashton Jeanty?
articles.headlineJa: レイダースのランニングゲームが苦戦している理由と、アシュトン・ジャンティの今後
articles.descriptionJa: レイダースは攻撃面で進歩を見せているが、ランニングゲームだけが課題となっている。ラスベガスとアシュトン・ジャンティに次なる展開はあるか？
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- The Las Vegas Raiders opened their Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs with plenty of momentum. Four plays in, and they already were on the scoreboard when quarterback Kirk Cousins threw a 27-yard touchdown pass to tight end Ian Thomas.

The Raiders tried to replicate that success on their second drive, but were unsuccessful.

With 2:17 to go in the first quarter and the game tied at seven, Cousins completed a 15-yard pass to tight end Michael Mayer, then coach Klint Kubiak turned to the run game to keep the chains moving, but they didn't. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. was stopped for a one-yard attempt before Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane wrapped up running back Ashton Jeanty for no gain. On third-and-9, Cousins threw an incomplete pass, which forced the Raiders to punt.

In the Raiders' 30-27 loss to the Chiefs last Sunday, they went toe-to-toe with a team that has won nine of the past 10 AFC West titles. But the Raiders' upset attempt failed because of more than a questionable fourth-down decision from Kubiak or Dareke Young's kick return fumble. For the third straight week, Las Vegas failed to establish a consistent run game, totaling 72 yards.

The Raiders have made significant offensive strides; they rank eighth in the league in points per game (28.7) and Cousins has thrown a league-high 11 touchdowns. However, their rushing attack has been a problem. Entering the season, the Raiders' run game was meant to be their biggest strength. Instead, their production has mirrored last year when they ranked last in nearly every rushing metric.

Multiple factors have contributed to Las Vegas' faulty rushing attack, from playcalling to Jeanty, their top running back and 2025 first-round pick, playing through an ankle injury. Jeanty was a limited participant in Thursday's practice due to an ankle and foot injury. If the Raiders want to show their strong first month wasn't a fluke, they will need to improve their rushing numbers, starting Sunday afternoon against the New England Patriots (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

"I think we've just got to be better. Simple as that," Jeanty said. "Make the plays that are out there. ... It starts with us. Starts with me. Got to break tackles and make bigger plays when they're available."

FIXING THE RUN game was a big part of the Raiders' preparation ahead of the season. In the past three seasons, Las Vegas ranked last in rushing yards per game (82.7) and yards per attempt (3.6).

This year was meant to be a different story. Jeanty was entering Year 2 and more experienced. Kubiak brought in a proven outside zone run scheme. The Raiders signed center Tyler Linderbaum, who is one of the better run blockers at his position. And Washington showed throughout training camp that he could be capable of being a reliable second option in the backfield.

articles.headline: How Saints can regroup, fix slow starts ahead of matchup with unbeaten Vikings
articles.description: New Orleans had a tough Week 4 loss to Atlanta, which also highlighted key deficiencies the Saints need to correct.
articles.headlineJa: セインツはどう立て直すべきか？無敗のバイキングス戦を前にスロースタートを修正する方法
articles.descriptionJa: ニューオーリンズは第4週にアトランタに手痛い敗戦を喫し、セインツが修正すべき重要な弱点が浮き彫りとなった。
articles.body:
METAIRIE, La. -- The bitterness of the New Orleans Saints' 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night will linger throughout a shortened week. 

That's exactly how Saints defensive end Chase Young wants it with the 4-0 Minnesota Vikings up next on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

"You should be upset," Young said Wednesday. "We didn't play to our standard, but the positive is seeing everybody come in today, how they're dealing with it. And that's what you want to see: dudes who have a sour taste in their mouth, dudes who are mad about it. I hope you mad. You get punched in your mouth, hopefully you ain't smiling."

Young said he was pleased with the response of his teammates this week as they figure out how to regroup on both sides of the ball before Sunday. While Young will be facing an offense that ranks 18th in scoring, the Saints' offense will go up against the NFL's best scoring defense and top pass rush. 

"They're undefeated, so that kind of speaks to the defense that they've had," tight end Juwan Johnson said. "[They] bring a large amount of exotic blitzes, exotic looks. You're going to get a lot of shell looks, you're going to get a bunch of different shell looks. The biggest part is just exploiting just the gaps in their defense ... just playing our ball. We know how to play.

"We just need to execute better."

The Saints (1-3) will be underdogs against a Vikings squad that Saints wideout Chris Olave said is "one of the best teams in the NFL." Olave noted in an interview with French media this week that the Vikings have a lot of stunts and blitzes that can be difficult to face.

"We're just going to have to put our best foot forward," he said.

"They're 4-0, we're 1-3. On paper it's a lopsided matchup, but at the end of the day we still have to go out there and play for 60 minutes."

Early mistakes doomed the Saints against the Falcons. The Saints allowed 205 yards on the ground after letting Bijan Robinson run 59 yards for a touchdown three plays into the game. The Saints rushed for only 50 yards as a team. 

That rushing output and the team's slow starts have gone hand in hand. The Saints have the third-fewest first-quarter points this season (six), compared with 39 in the fourth quarter, which is tied for the most in the league with the Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos. 

The Saints have rushed for more than 100 yards only once this season. 

"To be transparent, it's obvious that we've struggled running," Johnson said. "And I think we've been pretty good in the offseason just being dialed in on our keys and running the ball and it hasn't shown, but I think whenever we, and when we do well at running the ball, we're going to see an explosive amount of big plays just from our offense."

Part of the lack of run game comes from falling behind early, which has forced the Saints to pass more. Defensively, they've given up 32 points per game, last in the league, a difficult combination for offensive balance.

articles.body:
The Premier League is back for its first weekend of fixtures since Manchester City were found guilty of breaching its financial rules, a verdict they are appealing.

City travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday -- a blockbuster occasion after the clubs' history through some of the period impacted by an independent commission's findings.

- What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

But managers up and down the Premier League have already had their say when questioned about City's guilty verdict.

Mikel Arteta, Michael Carrick, Andoni Iraola, Roberto De Zerbi and Xabi Alonso are among the notable names who will speak in pre-match news conferences on Friday, and can expect to be quizzed about the charges.

City's Enzo Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola this summer, will also face the media.

Here, ESPN rounds up what managers have already said about City, and what they say throughout Friday's media duties...

articles.headline: Vincent Kompany 'proud' of Man City achievements despite guilty verdict over Premier League breaches
articles.description: Former Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany said he remains "proud" of the club's achievements during his time there despite the club being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィンセント・コンパニー、プレミアリーグ規則違反での有罪判決後もマン・シティの功績を「誇りに思う」と表明
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティの元キャプテン、ヴィンセント・コンパニーは、クラブが100件を超えるプレミアリーグの財務規則違反で有罪判決を受けたものの、自身の在籍期間におけるクラブの功績については引き続き「誇りに思う」と語った。
articles.body:
Former Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany said he remains "proud" of the club's achievements during his time there despite the club being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Kompany spent more than a decade with City between 2008 and 2019, lifting the Premier League trophy four times, also winning the FA Cup twice and the League Cup four times.

An independent commission has found that City broke financial rules across nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, which covers three of the Premier League titles Kompany won with City.

The Bayern Munich head coach said: "I played 11 years for the club. I've loved all of the years I played for the club and everything we achieved and done on the pitch, that's something I'm really proud of.

"Everything else, as a player you're not a part of that and right now as a coach of Bayern Munich I'm not too much occupied with that topic as I'm preparing the game next week and preparing the game we have tomorrow and everything I have as a coach."
